chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, that Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) wrote to him in a letter:
Be careful that you do not speak with a word of transgression ever, even if it pleases yourself and your clan.

key_terms.بَغْيٍ: Transgression, extravagance, or exceeding bounds in speech or action

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'kalamat bagh' refer to in Shia hadith literature regarding speech?
ai.summary: In this epistle to Misma'a ibn Sayyar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against *bagh* (transgression/extravagance in speech), a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethics as the precursor to broader moral decay. The Imam specifically targets the danger of self-satisfaction (*ta'ajjub al-nafs*) and tribal pride, which can embolden individuals to exceed proper bounds even when their words seem pleasing or justified. This advice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue) as a critical discipline for maintaining spiritual integrity amidst social validation.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Misma’a Abu Sayyar that Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him in a letter: ‘
Look (be careful) that you do not speak with a transgressing word, ever, and even if it astounds yourself and your clan’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once wrote a letter to me in which he had said, ‘
Keep in mind not to ever speak a tyrannical and transgressing word even though your own soul and tribe are more captivating to you.’”
